rationale: Calame et al. (2023) identified a total of 20 individuals with heterozygous de novo or rare DHX9 variants exhibiting a wide phenotypic spectrum that bifurcates based on variant domain and mechanism. Rather than all 20 individuals presenting with neurodevelopmental disorders (OMIM #620988), the cohort explicitly includes individuals with axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) driven by distinct missense variants in specific domains (such as winged helix and C-terminal RGG domains) that cause nucleolar accumulation rather than nuclear-cytoplasmic mislocalization or LoF-associated NDD phenotypes. Therefore, the denominator of individuals with core NDD phenotypes within the cohort of 20 is strictly less than 20/20.

evidence.text: Calame et al. (2023) reported 20 individuals with monoallelic DHX9 variants where phenotypes spanned from severe and mild neurodevelopmental disorders to adult-onset axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2), with CMT2-associated variants showing distinct functional cellular consequences.

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Using exome sequencing and family-based rare-variant analyses, we identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare, heterozygous missense or loss-of-function (LoF) DHX9 variant alleles. Phenotypes ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).

evidence.text: Variants in specific domains of DHX9, specifically the winged helix and C-terminal RGG domains, associate with hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy / Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 2 disease rather than central neurodevelopmental disorder phenotypes.

evidence.text: Neurological disorders caused by DHX9 gene pathogenicity present with distinct phenotypes, segregating into neurodevelopmental disorders affecting the central nervous system versus type 2 Charcot-Marie-Tooth distal symmetric peripheral polyneuropathy.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact breakdown of individuals presenting with pure NDD, pure CMT2, or overlapping central-peripheral nervous system phenotypes across an expanded multi-center DHX9 cohort?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether any CMT2-harboring individuals manifest subclinical or subtle developmental delay is essential to refine HPO terms for diagnostic gene panels.

new_directions.question_text: Do downstream transcriptional and R-loop profiles differ between fibroblasts from individuals with DHX9-associated NDD versus DHX9-associated CMT2?
new_directions.rationale: Determining functional molecular biomarkers will help classify variants of uncertain significance into either NDD or peripheral neuropathy disease mechanisms.
